rows.35:124c:
"...With all this, I think we can put together an interesting school paper.
So I'd like to bring things to a close here..."{p}
rows.35:186c:
{f:I|I} decided to help myself without holding back.
Everyone took whatever they liked.
From among them, {f:I|I} chose the orange juice.
One hundred percent juice.
I opened the cap and brought it to my mouth.
...Mmm, {f:that's good|delicious}.
Maybe because I'd been so tense, the nicely chilled orange juice felt {f:great|so nice} going down.{p}
rows.35:25b0:
Shindo, you know Iwayama, right?
Him. You know, that guy.
The one who's good with his hands.
Or you could say he's quick with his hands.
I bet he'd go far if he became a thief... wait, that's a crime, huh.{p}
rows.35:2688:
Shirai's famous for how he guards his keys.
There are three keys just for the storeroom, and the guy's gone and stuck them in a safe, inside a locked cabinet.
Truth is, I'd been working on this plan for about half a year now.
If I uncovered Shirai's secret, that alone would be a guaranteed scoop.
Honestly, I wanted to run it big as a front-page exclusive, not as one piece of some school seven wonders feature like this.
But while I was dragging my feet with one thing and another, this seven wonders project tied to the demolition of the old school building came up, so for me, it's all ending up a bit of a letdown.{p}
rows.35:301c:
And I wondered what on earth was going on.
The room looked like it went pretty far back, but it was pitch-black and I couldn't see a thing.
There seemed to be all kinds of stuff cluttered around, but none of it made any sense.
Walking around carelessly would be dangerous.
If I could just get the light on, I'd be able to see clearly.
I was desperately trying to find the switch.
That's when it happened.
Behind me, I heard the sound of something falling over.{p}
rows.35:317c:
I looked, and there was Iwayama, collapsed on the floor, gasping like he was in pain.
"Hey, Iwayama."
"...Hino. I feel sick.
This room stinks. I can't... take it..."
The formalin stink was so strong that the jerk Iwayama got drunk on it.{p}
rows.35:4f10:
"Even like that, they're alive.
And now they're my comrades.
The only difference is whether you keep a human shape like this or not."
Then he looked at {f:me|me} once more and laughed.
"...Whether you get to keep the shape you've got now probably depends on you.
If you fuse well, let's make more comrades together.
Hee hee hee..."
Then he turned his eyes the opposite way from the living lumps of flesh.{p}
rows.35:599c:
...But there's a downside too.
You stop being yourself.
Once this bacterium settles into your body, it completely takes over your will and your body.
All your memories and feelings up to now disappear.
That's the only shame of it.
I'm going to end up like that soon, too.
In about ten days, I'll be completely reborn as a new life-form.
...I'll stop being me.
That's so frustrating.
And I hate it.{p}
rows.35:6b24:
Don't lie to me.
With your eyes shining like that, you can't tell me you're 'not curious.'
Come on, be honest.{p}You really are curious about what Shirai's doing, aren't you?
rows.35:6bdc:
Huh. Is that so?
Maybe you're not cut out for the newspaper club, huh?{p}
rows.35:7b74:
Hino came closer to {f:me|me}.
Was it just my imagination{f:?|?}
The smell seemed to be getting stronger...
A smell like something rotting, one that stung my eyes.
"Do I smell that bad?"
Before I knew it, Hino was standing right in front of me.
I was right, this smell was coming from Hino!
{f:I|I} couldn't say a word anymore, and Hino grinned at me.
"Iwayama got eaten..........by me."{p}
rows.35:918c:
Then, to look for the light switch, I felt my way along the wall.
Slowly, slowly...
As before, my hand never touched anything like a switch.
Then I wondered.
What was that baby crying earlier...?
Just as I thought that and went to take a step...{p}
